predictions.reasoning: This market concerns the 2028 presidential outcome for a single candidate (AOC) more than three years out. A 12-hour shift in her implied win probability carries essentially no information that liquid markets would price today. Even if AOC were viewed as market-unfriendly (progressive tax/regulation agenda), the time horizon is so distant, the base probability so low, and the resolution so uncertain that no meaningful discounting flows into current equity prices within a 12h window. There is no credible mechanistic link strong enough to produce a >=700bps move.

evidence_used: Market question targets 2028 US Presidential Election, over three years from any plausible signal date
Single-candidate binary with structurally low base probability
No region/topic specifics beyond US elections
12h prediction window versus multi-year resolution horizon
uncertainty_notes: Long-dated political probability shifts rarely map to same-day asset moves
Prediction markets on distant elections are thin and noisy
Any equity reaction to a progressive candidate would be gradual and dwarfed by macro factors over such a horizon

llm_justification.summary: The market asks whether AOC wins the 2028 presidential election — an outcome over three years away and structurally low probability. A 12-hour swing in her implied odds would not credibly transmit into liquid public-market prices within the same window; the time horizon, low base rate, and market thinness break any mechanistic link. Best mapped as a non-signal: unclear direction, negligible expected move, very low confidence, and well below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: No imminent, market-moving political catalyst is embedded in the question
Equity markets discount distant, low-probability political outcomes minimally
The proxy (SPY) is only weakly and indirectly exposed to this event
failure_modes: A dramatic real-world catalyst (e.g., AOC announcing candidacy tied to a broader Democratic realignment) could move markets, but that would be public, not leaked
The chosen proxy is too broad and diluted to reflect a single-candidate 2028 shift
The market move may simply be low-liquidity noise with zero informational content
Reversal is likely as speculative long-dated odds mean-revert
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
